tables.caption: Table 1 Composition of the selected data sources. Split columns report image counts.

Table 2 Cross-model mask AP comparison on AgriParcel-MS. Values are percentages and rows are ordered by AP50–95. All six models use the training and test splits and common training budget in Section 2.6.1. Test results cover 2,000 images; AP summarizes mask overlap across confidence thresholds.

Table 3 Fixed-threshold detection, count, and area results at confidence 0.25. Detection and area-relative-error metrics are percentages. Small parcels have area ≤ 1,024 pixels in the 640 × 640 evaluation grid. Count MAE covers all images; matched-parcel MAPE excludes unmatched instances. WAPE and net bias use foreground-union areas, and net bias retains its sign. Bold indicates better performance: higher detection metrics, lower error metrics, and smaller absolute net area bias.

Table 4 Module ablation and boundary structure. ✓ and × indicate enabled and disabled modules. A = BDS, B = BAPS, and C = RBQS; the all-disabled row is the baseline and the all-enabled row is FieldBCQ. Values are percentages except score–IoU ECE (0–1). P and R use the evaluator-selected best-F1 operating point; mAP denotes mask AP across confidence thresholds. Boundary-F1, merge rate, oversegmentation rate, and ECE use confidence 0.25. Matching uses mask IoU ≥ 0.50 and a boundary tolerance of 2 pixels on the 640 × 640 grid. Each configuration uses one checkpoint with training seed 0. Native F1 and AP75 are provided in Table S1. Bold indicates the best value in each metric column.

Table 5 Same-checkpoint comparison of class-only and joint scoring. Both conditions use the complete model’s trained weights; class-only scoring disables inference fusion. AP is native; other metrics use confidence 0.25. Differences are calculated from unrounded results and expressed in percentage points except for ECE. Bold indicates better performance.
Table S1. Complete native operating-point and mask AP results for the eight configurations.
Table S2. Source-group segmentation results at confidence 0.25.
